Labour Party (UK) }} The '''2026 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election''' will take place on Thursday 7 May 2026, alongside [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]]. One third of the 60 members of [[North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council]] in [[Tyne and Wear]] will be elected. ==Background== North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council was created in 1974. [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] saw early success, controlling the council (apart from a brief period of no overall control [[1986 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election|1986]] to [[1987 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election|1987]]) from its creation until [[2004 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election|2004]], when the council fell into [[no overall control]].{{cite web |title=BBC News - Election 2011 - England council elections - North Tyneside |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/special/election2011/council/html/ck.stm |website=BBC News |access-date=10 January 2026}} That election also saw the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] become the largest party on the council, which was maintained until [[2010 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election|2010]].{{cite web |title=North Tyneside Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=https://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/North-Tyneside-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=10 January 2026}} The Conservatives additionally formed the only non-Labour majority administration following the [[2008 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election|2008 election]]. Labour have formed majority administrations since retaking control in [[2011 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election|2011]], with the Conservatives acting as the principal opposition. The [[2024 North Tyneside Metropolitan Borough Council election|2024 election]] used a new set of ward boundaries - as such, this election will be for the councillors elected with the fewest votes in each of the 30 three-member wards.[https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2024/138/made The North Tyneside (Electoral Changes) Order 2024] Labour will be defending 17 seats, the Conservatives will be defending 2, and [[Independent politician|independents]] will be defending 1.{{cite news |last1=Shakespeare |first1=Austen |last2=Holland |first2=Daniel |title=North Tyneside local election results 2024 in full |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/north-east-news/north-tyneside-election-results-2024-29091987 |access-date=10 January 2026 |work=Chronicle Live |date=4 May 2024 |language=en}} ==Summary== === Council composition === {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2024 election ! colspan="3" | Before 2026 election ! colspan="3" | After 2026 election |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
